parts.content:
Best move: **b7**.

Briefly: **b7 doesn’t give White an immediate corner**, and it seems to take control of the lower-left region while limiting White’s good replies. The key endgame feature is **corner access/mobility**, not just the number flipped right now.

args.question: Looking back, why was White stuck passing so many times in a row near the end? I don't fully get why it couldn't move even though it had way more discs than me.

parts.content:
White had to pass because in Othello a move is legal only if it **flanks at least one opponent disc** between the disc you place and another of your discs; just having lots of discs doesn’t matter if no empty square creates a flip.  

The deciding feature was **mobility**: near the end, your moves left White with many discs but **no legal flanking lines**, so White’s turn was skipped until a later Black move created one. That’s why endgames often favor moves that leave the opponent **few or zero legal replies**, even if they don’t flip many discs immediately.
That clears it up — so it's really about boxing in their options, not just flipping the most pieces each turn. Let me ask one more thing.

args.question: Was there a risk in playing a3 before a1 - like could White have had some move in between that I got lucky avoiding, or was that sequence actually forced/safe?

parts.content: It was **safe/forced**, not just luck. The deciding feature was **White’s mobility**: after your **a3**, White still had **no legal flanking move**, so it had to pass and you could take **a1** next. In general playing near an empty corner can be dangerous, but here the pass meant White never got a turn to use it.
Good, glad to hear it was solid and not just luck. Alright — final score stands at 41 to 23, Black wins. Thanks for talking me through the tricky spots along the way, this was a fun one!
